inputs.seed_note: no random numbers are drawn in P6

evidence_class: independent of App. L's disk in the profile losses; it shares the momentum theory (spec P6). The section data and the validation propeller are measured open data (NACA Reports 259 and 640)

tr640.title: The Aerodynamic Characteristics of Full-Scale Propellers Having 2, 3, and 4 Blades of Clark Y and R.A.F. 6 Airfoil Sections
tr640.used_for: validation row 5: the measured propeller (blade geometry, Fig. 2; efficiency, Fig. 12)
tr640.why_this_one: Of the three candidates (TR-640, TR-650, TR-642; NTRS metadata of all three was read) TR-640 has a three-blade propeller, prints the blade-form curves and the efficiency curves of that propeller, and was opened first. TR-650 and TR-642 were not downloaded.

tr259.title: Characteristics of Propeller Sections Tested in the Variable Density Wind Tunnel
tr259.used_for: section lift and drag of the blade elements (data/task12/pd_p6_tr259_sections.yaml)

acr4b04.number: NACA ACR 4B04 (reissued as a NACA Wartime Report)
acr4b04.title: Comparison of Calculated and Experimental Propeller Characteristics for Four-, Six-, and Eight-Blade Single-Rotating Propellers
acr4b04.used_for: the open statement of strip theory with a correction for a finite number of blades, recorded before use (spec P6 step 2). Its pages 4 to 6 (printed) state the method "as used by Lock": the element solidity sigma = B b/(2 pi r), the inflow angle from tan(eps) = sigma C_L/(4 F sin(phi)) with F the Goldstein factor read from a chart, and tan(gamma) = C_D/C_L. Only the first 8 PDF pages were read.
acr4b04.what_it_does_not_give: It takes F from Goldstein's chart, not from Prandtl's closed form, and it writes the light-loading (vortex) form, not the momentum balance per annulus. prelim/bem.py writes the momentum balance itself (it follows from Mattingly (L.3) and (L.5) applied to one annulus) and uses Prandtl's closed form for F. No opened open source prints Prandtl's F; it is written from its textbook definition and that is listed as an assumption in the report.

opened_and_not_used.why: names Glauert's and Adkins and Liebeck's strip theory (PDF pages 53 to 54) but prints no equation of it

library_figure.what: Mattingly, Aircraft Engine Design 2nd ed., Fig. L.5, p. 616: element efficiency against inflow angle, (1 - a')/(1 + a) = 0.8
library_figure.page_opened: 2026-11-27, uv run alex page mattingly-aircraft-engine-design 616 (rendered page, 1600 px long side)
library_figure.axis_check: the frame's 1.0 and 0.0 lines are 500 px apart; the drawn C_L/C_D = infinity line reads 0.800

tr640_test.propeller: Navy design, drawing 5868-9, Clark Y sections, 3 blades (printed page 1)
tr640_test.body: geared Curtiss Conqueror engine in a liquid-cooled engine nacelle, 43 in deep, 38 in wide, 126 in long (printed page 2)
tr640_test.tunnel: N.A.C.A. 20-foot wind tunnel, open throat, up to about 115 miles per hour (printed pages 1 and 2)
tr640_test.rpm_note: held below 115 mph tunnel speed; above, the tunnel speed is held and rpm is about 1,000/(V/nD) (printed page 3)
tr640_test.efficiency_definition: eta = C_T (V/nD)/C_P with the effective thrust T_e = T - delta D, shaft tension less the change of body drag due to the slipstream (printed page 3): a propulsive efficiency of the propeller and engine unit, not of the isolated propeller.
tr640_test.precision: repeat tests usually checked first tests within about 1 percent (printed page 3)

blade_geometry.figure: Figure 2, printed page 2 (PDF page 6): blade-form curves for propellers 5868-9, 5868-R6 and 37-3647
blade_geometry.scan: PDF page 6 rendered at 300 dpi (pdftoppm -r 300), figure crop x 170 to 1299, y 1435 to 2801
blade_geometry.grid: vertical lines every 0.05 in r/R; horizontal lines every 0.005 in b/D, 0.02 in h/b, 0.1 in p/D; the page is skewed by about 3 px in 1,000
blade_geometry.readings: eye_tile: by eye on 4x and 5x enlarged tiles, the curve where it crosses the station's grid line, against a mark drawn at a trial value. code: prelim/p6_figure_read.py, a straight line through the curve's crossings of up to ten columns 8 to 20 px either side of the grid line; null where the fit landed on a neighbouring curve or a label (seen on the tile) or found fewer than four crossings. eye_crop: the first reading, by eye on 2x enlarged crops, used as the second reading where the code has none.
blade_geometry.value_rule: value = mean of eye_tile and the second reading (code, or eye_crop where code is null)
blade_geometry.uncertainty_rule: half the difference of the two readings, at least 1.5 px: 0.00015 in b/D, 0.0006 in h/b, 0.003 in p/D
blade_geometry.h_over_b_note: Inboard of r/R 0.35 the thickness ratio is above 0.20, the thickest section with data; the curve leaves the plot (above 0.44) near r/R 0.29. No value is read there and the model takes the 0.20 section.
blade_geometry.pitch_set_25_note: p/D of the curve marked 25 deg (set 25 deg at 0.75R); the blade angle is atan(p/D / (pi r/R))
blade_geometry.pitch_set_15_note: the curve marked 15 deg, read as a cross-check of the twist only: [r/R, null, code, eye_crop]
blade_geometry.not_read: the 35 deg pitch curve (read in part by eye only, not used); r/R beyond 0.95 (the plot ends at 0.975)

efficiency.figure: Figure 12, printed page 7 (PDF page 11): efficiency curves for propeller 5868-9, Clark Y section, 3 blades
efficiency.scan: PDF page 11 rendered at 300 dpi, figure crop x 171 to 2332, y 2360 to 3249
efficiency.grid: lines every 0.1 in V/nD and in eta. The page is skewed (about 20 px in 1,600) and the frame's top and bottom lines are not on the pitch of the inner lines, so the scale is taken from the 0.1 and 0.9 lines.
efficiency.stations: Chosen before any calculation, where the curve is above 0.5 (it is drawn solid there; dashed below about V/nD 0.25). 15 deg: every 0.05 from 0.30 to 0.75. 25 deg: 0.45 (the lowest 0.05 station above 0.5), every 0.1 from 0.5 to 1.0, and every 0.05 from 1.0 to 1.25, where the curve turns down.
efficiency.readings: code: prelim/p6_figure_read.py, a straight line through the curve's crossings of up to ten columns 8 to 24 px either side of the station. eye_tile: by eye on 4x enlarged tiles against a mark at a trial value.
efficiency.value_rule: value = mean of the two readings
efficiency.uncertainty_rule: half the difference of the two readings, at least 0.004 (the drawn line is about 3 px wide)
efficiency.judged_rule: a station is judged in row 5 if its reading uncertainty is at most 0.015, half the row's tolerance
efficiency.note_1_25: At V/nD 1.25 the 25 deg curve falls at about 7 in eta per unit of V/nD; the code's straight-line fit is biased high by the curvature and the two readings differ by 0.039. By the judged rule the station is reported and not judged.
efficiency.note_1_20: At V/nD 1.20 the code reading depends on the trial value that picks the curve: 0.7561 (recorded, trial 0.747) and 0.7621 (trial 0.7561, what prelim/p6_figure_read.py prints now). The eye reading is 0.7576.
